source.title: Running Video Analysis

observations.observation: Runner filmed from behind on treadmill, with alternating foot strikes visible.
Rear-view analysis overlays a body centerline and discusses whether the feet cross it and whether hips remain level.
Side close-up discusses overstriding, showing a forward foot far in front of the body and its effect on impact.

source.usage: Motion and gait reference only; no YouTube frames copied or downloaded.

generation.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: ORIGINAL 4x4 running animation contact sheet for a fitness app, one image containing sixteen equally sized consecutive pose panels, read left to right then top to bottom. Clean high-quality realistic sports instructional photography / consistent stylized 3D look. In every panel EXACTLY the same full-body adult runner in heather gray short-sleeve T-shirt and dark charcoal running shorts, same side / slight three-quarter side camera, body facing SCREEN RIGHT, stationary relative to the frame, centered and fully within panel including head, hands, feet and ground line. Plain light neutral studio background, same floor baseline and camera angle. Shoes have permanent anatomical markers: runner's LEFT ANKLE AND LEFT SHOE are vivid ORANGE in EVERY frame; runner's RIGHT ANKLE AND RIGHT SHOE are vivid BLUE in EVERY frame. Correct markers remain attached to the same anatomical legs even as legs overlap. This is forward RUNNING motion, anatomically plausible and cyclic, both legs alternately taking weight, never reversing like a pendulum. Sixteen distinct poses sample precisely ONE FULL STRIDE of the same runner, with explicit visible sequence: panel 1 left/orange foot initial contact under pelvis and right/blue leg behind; 2 orange loading with blue recovery forward; 3 orange midstance under pelvis, blue knee advancing; 4 orange late stance heel lifted, blue knee ahead; 5 orange toe-off behind and blue foot reaching ahead; 6 both feet airborne, blue ahead, orange behind; 7 airborne descending with blue preparing to land; 8 right/BLUE initial ground contact under pelvis, orange trailing airborne; 9 blue loading with orange recovering forward; 10 blue midstance under pelvis, orange knee advancing; 11 blue late stance heel lifted, orange knee ahead; 12 blue toe-off behind, orange reaching ahead; 13 both feet airborne, orange ahead, blue behind; 14 airborne descending, orange preparing to land; 15 orange very near landing, blue lifted behind; 16 orange contact near same state as panel 1 to close loop. Opposite arms counter-swing naturally. Show CLEAR stance and airborne phases, distinct right and left ground contacts and progressive leg motion. Uniform panels with thin subtle white gutter only. NO text, numbers, arrows, captions, logos, treadmill, ghosting, duplicated body parts, extra limbs, cropping, swapped colors, reverse running, or repeated same lead leg. Make framing generous enough that full body and shoes are never cut off.
generation.first_candidate_issue: Panels 9 and 10 showed two blue shoes, breaking permanent leg identity.
generation.revision_prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: the provided 4-by-4 running sprite/contact sheet. Preserve EVERYTHING exactly: panel layout, same runner, body poses, gray shirt, dark shorts, fixed camera, all background and floor, all other 14 panels, lighting, 1254x1254 square composition. ONLY correct the colored shoe/ankle identity in ROW 3, COLUMNS 1 and 2 (panels 9 and 10, counting left-to-right top-to-bottom). Those two panels mistakenly show two BLUE shoes. In each of those two panels, recolor the runner's ANATOMIC LEFT shoe and its ankle sock/orange marker to vivid ORANGE, matching the orange shoe color elsewhere on the sheet; leave the ANATOMIC RIGHT shoe vivid BLUE. The left leg in panels 9 and 10 is the forward bent knee/raised foot swinging in front of the blue support foot; recolor THAT FORWARD RAISED shoe and ankle ORANGE in BOTH panels. Keep the blue support shoe untouched. No changes to poses or any other panels. This is a strict localized color correction, not regeneration.
generation.second_candidate_issue: Panel 7 orange shoe corrected, but arms still appeared nearly frozen across the cycle.
generation.final_revision_prompt: Precise-object-edit of supplied 16-frame 4x4 running contact sheet. The current error is that THE ARMS ARE IDENTICAL in every panel. This must be visually repaired; make arms change pose significantly across the cycle while everything below the shoulders remains exactly the same. Preserve 4x4 layout, 16 distinct chronological leg poses, and EVERY shoe exactly: one ORANGE left shoe and one BLUE right shoe in all panels, same background/camera/runner/clothing. Animate the ARMS as a real counter-swinging cycle. The very visible arm on the runner's near side, presently stuck backward with hand at hip in ALL frames, needs to sweep forward between frames 5–10: move its ELBOW toward the front of ribcage and its FIST ahead of sternum at chest height in frames 7–9. At the same time the other far-side arm that is currently stuck forward with fist near chest must sweep backward, fist beside rear hip in frames 7–9. Between frames 1–4 and 13–16 reverse those positions: near side fist beside rear hip, far side fist ahead of chest. Frames 5–6 and 11–12 are smooth transitions with both arms near mid-swing. This should create an OBVIOUS reversal of which arm is in front halfway through, clearly visible even in thumbnail. Exactly two arms with correct shoulder attachments, human anatomy, bent elbows around 90 degrees, no ghost limbs. Do not recreate or crop legs, shoes, head, camera, or floor; no text, labels, numbers, arrows.
generation.third_candidate_issue: Near-side arm returned backward two frames too late relative to left/orange leg forward swing.
generation.final_timing_prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Strictly edit ONLY the ARMS in row 3, columns 1 and 2 (panels 9 and 10) of the supplied 4x4 running sheet. In those two panels the LEFT/ORANGE leg has swung FORWARD with a bent raised orange shoe, so the left/near arm must now swing BACK with fist near rear hip, while the opposite right/far arm swings FORWARD with fist near lower chest. Currently their arm arrangement still matches the previous blue-forward phase; reverse their arm positions in these two panels only. Preserve every other detail in every panel exactly: runner, 4x4 layout, leg poses and shoes, one orange and one blue shoe in each cell, body orientation, clothing, faces, background, lighting, floor. Exactly two anatomically attached arms, no extra limbs, no cropping or text. Make row3 columns1–2 arms match the counter-swing posture of row3 column3 and row3 column4.
generation.visual_audit: Checked every panel: each has exactly one orange left shoe and one blue right shoe. Opposite arms visibly change anatomical lead during blue-right-leg-forward panels 6 through 8, then return during orange-left-leg-forward panels 9 through 16. Right and left support phases and airborne transitions are visible.
